title: Why we need to protect polar bears
titleCn: Why we need to protect polar bears
subject: reading

paragraphs.text: Why we need to protect polar bears

Polar bears are being increasingly threatened by the effects of climate change, but their disappearance could have far-reaching consequences. They are uniquely adapted to the extreme conditions of the Arctic Circle, where temperatures can reach −40°C. One reason for this is that they have up to 11 centimetres of fat underneath their skin. Humans with comparative levels of adipose tissue would be considered obese and would be likely to suffer from diabetes and heart disease. Yet the polar bear experiences no such consequences.

A 2014 study by Shi Ping Liu and colleagues sheds light on this mystery. They compared the genetic structure of polar bears with that of their closest relatives from a warmer climate, the brown bears. This allowed them to determine the genes that have allowed polar bears to survive in one of the toughest environments on Earth. Liu and his colleagues found the polar bears had a gene known as APoB, which reduces levels of low-density lipoproteins (LDLs) – a form of ‘bad’ cholesterol. In humans, mutations of this gene are associated with increased risk of heart disease. Polar bears may therefore be an important study model to understand heart disease in humans.

The genome of the polar bear may also provide the solution for another condition, one that particularly affects our older generation: osteoporosis. This is a disease where bones show reduced density, usually caused by insufficient exercise, reduced calcium intake or food starvation. Bone tissue is constantly being remodelled, meaning that bone is added or removed, depending on nutrient availability and the stress that the bone is under. Female polar bears, however, undergo extreme conditions during every pregnancy. Once autumn comes around, these females will dig maternity dens in the snow and will remain there throughout the winter, both before and after the birth of their cubs. This process results in about six months of fasting, where the female bears have to keep themselves and their cubs alive, depleting their own calcium and calorie reserves. Despite this, their bones remain strong and dense.

Physiologists Alanda Lennox and Allen Goodship found an explanation for this paradox in 2008. They discovered that pregnant bears were able to increase the density of their bones before they started to build their dens. In addition, six months later, when they finally emerged from the den with their cubs, there was no evidence of significant loss of bone density. Hibernating brown bears do not have this capacity and must therefore resort to major bone reformation in the following spring. If the mechanism of bone remodelling in polar bears can be understood, many bedridden humans, and even astronauts, could potentially benefit.

The medical benefits of the polar bear for humanity certainly have their importance in our conservation efforts, but these should not be the only factors taken into consideration. We tend to want to protect animals we think are intelligent and possess emotions, such as elephants and primates. Bears, on the other hand, seem to be perceived as stupid and in many cases violent. And yet anecdotal evidence from the field challenges those assumptions, suggesting for example that polar bears have good problem-solving abilities. A male bear called GoGo in Tennoji Zoo, Osaka, has even been observed making use of a tool to manipulate his environment. The bear used a tree branch on multiple occasions to dislodge a piece of meat hung out of his reach. Problem-solving ability has also been witnessed in wild polar bears, although not as obviously as with GoGo. A calculated move by a male bear involved running and jumping onto barrels in an attempt to get to a photographer standing on a platform four metres high.

In other studies, such as one by Alison Ames in 2008, polar bears showed deliberate and focussed manipulation. For example, Ames observed bears putting objects in piles and then knocking them over in what appeared to be a game. The study demonstrates that bears are capable of agile and thought-out behaviours. These examples suggest bears have greater creativity and problem-solving abilities than previously thought.

As for emotions, while the evidence is once again anecdotal, many bears have been seen to hit out at ice and snow – seemingly out of frustration – when they have just missed out on a kill. Moreover, polar bears can form unusual relationships with other species, including playing with the dogs used to pull sleds in the Arctic. Remarkably, one hand-raised polar bear called Agee has formed a close relationship with her owner Mark Dumas to the point where they even swim together. This is even more astonishing since polar bears are known to actively hunt humans in the wild.

If climate change were to lead to their extinction, this would mean the loss not only of potential breakthroughs in human medicine, but more importantly, the disappearance of an intelligent, majestic animal.

groups.instruction:
Questions 1–7

Do the following statements agree with the information given in Reading Passage 1?

In questions 1–7, choose

TRUE if the statement agrees with the information

FALSE if the statement contradicts the information

NOT GIVEN if there is no information on this

questions.prompt: Polar bears suffer from various health problems due to the build-up of fat under their skin.
questions.explanation:
译文：北极熊会由于皮下脂肪堆积而遭受各种健康问题的困扰。

作为全文第一个题型中的第一道题，本题在第一自然段里即可凭借题干中的fat或skin进行轻松定位。不过包含这两个关键词的句子并没有提及这些皮下脂肪是否会给北极熊带来各种疾病，因此考生还需耐心继续阅读文章、寻找更多解题依据。

虽然接下来的原文句中使用了adipose“脂蛋白”这个比较生僻的词汇来替换了fat，但考生如果是在用平行阅读的方法顺序阅读每句，就不难从上下文中推知此处的adipose就是指向上一句里的fat，这个生僻词并不会给考生顺利阅读文意和解题带来障碍。真正需要考生关注的语言细节，反而是这个句子里的虚拟语气would的用法，意为“如果人类也有这么多脂肪则可能会如何如何”，其实已经在暗示着真正有着这么多脂肪的北极熊其实并不会如何如何。最后一句开头的Yet则更是进一步加强了这个意义，考生即使在读完前两句后仍觉得缺乏明显针对北极熊的说明，看过了完整的第三句之后，应当也能顺利得出答案为FALSE。

questions.prompt: The study done by Liu and his colleagues compared different groups of polar bears.
questions.explanation:
译文：Liu及其团队所做的研究比较了几个不同的北极熊群。

本题的定位极其容易：无论是作为主语的Liu and colleagues，还是谓语动词compared，全部在原文中原词重现。但根据文中具体给出的信息，他们所比较的对象是北极熊和其近亲：棕熊，而非在北极熊这一个物种内部比较不同的群组，因此原文信息否定掉了题干信息，答案应为FALSE。

questions.prompt: Liu and colleagues were the first researchers to compare polar bears and brown bears genetically.
questions.explanation:
译文：Liu及其团队是第一批将北极熊与棕熊从基因角度做比较的研究者。

如果从“依据题干信息回原文定位”这个角度来看，本题的定位紧依上一道题，也是在说北极熊与棕熊之间的比较。然而Liu的团队是否为业内第一？耐心往下看便会得知：原文并没有在这个方面给出任何进一步的信息，因此答案为NOT GIVEN。

需要特别提醒的是：由于判断题天然包含NOT GIVEN这个选项，所以目标获取高分的考生在做题时，最理想的做法是“一次对比两道题”。以本题为例，考生在每次对比原文、查找是否提及题干信息“第一次”的同时，可以也查看下一道题的题干。如果原文中虽然没有包含第3题的信息、但却出现了第4题的内容，则可以及时止损，完成第4题的解答且第3题的答案很可能为NOT GIVEN，因为判断题为顺序出题的题型。反之，如果一次只专注于寻找和解答一道题目，则一旦此题因为答案为NOT GIVEN而并没有在原文中被提及，考生就有可能在寻找本题的过程中已经遇到了后面的题目而不自知，造成不必要的回读和浪费时间。

questions.prompt: Polar bears are able to control their levels of ‘bad’ cholesterol by genetic means.
questions.explanation:
译文：北极熊能够通过基因手段控制自己的“坏”胆固醇水平。

本题的定位和解题都极其容易。首先，凭借题干中的‘bad’ cholesterol，可以直接依靠原词重现定位到原文相应出题句；其次，定位句本身包含了可以得出答案的全部信息，考生只需看懂此句即可顺利解答，无需再看其他原文部分；此外，原文句本身也足够简单：主干表明北极熊确实拥有某种基因，which引导的从句进一步说明这种基因的功用是reduce某种物质的水平，而破折号后面的内容更是直接给这种物质定性为“‘bad’ cholesterol”。综上，考生可以毫不犹豫地得出正确答案为TRUE。

questions.prompt: Female polar bears are able to survive for about six months without food.
questions.explanation:
译文：雌性北极熊可以在没有食物的条件下生存约六个月。

本题可以利用题干中的数字信息six months轻松定位到相应原文出处。虽然题干中的survive...without food在原文中替换成了fasting（禁食，挨饿）这个略显生僻的对应词，但是结合整句表达的信息，不难看出是在说“不吃东西也能活这么久”，从而得出答案为TRUE。

questions.prompt: It was found that the bones of female polar bears were very weak when they came out of their dens in spring.
questions.explanation:
译文：当雌性北极熊在春季从自己的巢穴里现身时，它们的骨骼被发现非常脆弱。

本题的定位紧挨上一题，定位句开头第一个词Despite其实已经为后面的意思表达奠定了基调。上一句说“这些雌熊已经挨饿了六个月”，这个表达的正常推理逻辑应该是一些并不美好的结果；但下一句开头却说“尽管如此”，可见话锋即将出现转折，结果应该也没那么糟。读完全句则更加可以明确得知：它们的骨骼仍然强壮又紧密（strong and dense），由此可得答案应为FALSE。

questions.prompt: The polar bear’s mechanism for increasing bone density could also be used by people one day.
questions.explanation:
译文：北极熊用以增加骨骼密度的机制有可能某天也为人类所用。

本题的定位难度在此部分判断题中算是略高，但总体而言仍不算难题。在解答完上一道题后，考生只需按照原文顺序向下阅读，即可在第四段第二句找到“增加骨骼密度”这个信息；然而此句并没有提及这种机制是否可以为人所用，考生需耐心继续向后文寻找，才能在第四段最后一句中看到对题干信息进行同义表述的内容，从而得出答案为TRUE。

People think of bears as unintelligent and [8] ______. However, this may not be correct. For example:

articleHtml:
Why we need to protect polar bears

Polar bears are being increasingly threatened by the effects of climate change, but their disappearance could have far-reaching consequences. They are uniquely adapted to the extreme conditions of the Arctic Circle, where temperatures can reach −40°C. One reason for this is that they have up to 11 centimetres of fat underneath their skin. Humans with comparative levels of adipose tissue would be considered obese and would be likely to suffer from diabetes and heart disease. Yet the polar bear experiences no such consequences.

A 2014 study by Shi Ping Liu and colleagues sheds light on this mystery. They compared the genetic structure of polar bears with that of their closest relatives from a warmer climate, the brown bears. This allowed them to determine the genes that have allowed polar bears to survive in one of the toughest environments on Earth. Liu and his colleagues found the polar bears had a gene known as APoB, which reduces levels of low-density lipoproteins (LDLs) – a form of ‘bad’ cholesterol. In humans, mutations of this gene are associated with increased risk of heart disease. Polar bears may therefore be an important study model to understand heart disease in humans.

The genome of the polar bear may also provide the solution for another condition, one that particularly affects our older generation: osteoporosis. This is a disease where bones show reduced density, usually caused by insufficient exercise, reduced calcium intake or food starvation. Bone tissue is constantly being remodelled, meaning that bone is added or removed, depending on nutrient availability and the stress that the bone is under. Female polar bears, however, undergo extreme conditions during every pregnancy. Once autumn comes around, these females will dig maternity dens in the snow and will remain there throughout the winter, both before and after the birth of their cubs. This process results in about six months of fasting, where the female bears have to keep themselves and their cubs alive, depleting their own calcium and calorie reserves. Despite this, their bones remain strong and dense.

Physiologists Alanda Lennox and Allen Goodship found an explanation for this paradox in 2008. They discovered that pregnant bears were able to increase the density of their bones before they started to build their dens. In addition, six months later, when they finally emerged from the den with their cubs, there was no evidence of significant loss of bone density. Hibernating brown bears do not have this capacity and must therefore resort to major bone reformation in the following spring. If the mechanism of bone remodelling in polar bears can be understood, many bedridden humans, and even astronauts, could potentially benefit.

The medical benefits of the polar bear for humanity certainly have their importance in our conservation efforts, but these should not be the only factors taken into consideration. We tend to want to protect animals we think are intelligent and possess emotions, such as elephants and primates. Bears, on the other hand, seem to be perceived as stupid and in many cases violent. And yet anecdotal evidence from the field challenges those assumptions, suggesting for example that polar bears have good problem-solving abilities. A male bear called GoGo in Tennoji Zoo, Osaka, has even been observed making use of a tool to manipulate his environment. The bear used a tree branch on multiple occasions to dislodge a piece of meat hung out of his reach. Problem-solving ability has also been witnessed in wild polar bears, although not as obviously as with GoGo. A calculated move by a male bear involved running and jumping onto barrels in an attempt to get to a photographer standing on a platform four metres high.

In other studies, such as one by Alison Ames in 2008, polar bears showed deliberate and focussed manipulation. For example, Ames observed bears putting objects in piles and then knocking them over in what appeared to be a game. The study demonstrates that bears are capable of agile and thought-out behaviours. These examples suggest bears have greater creativity and problem-solving abilities than previously thought.

As for emotions, while the evidence is once again anecdotal, many bears have been seen to hit out at ice and snow – seemingly out of frustration – when they have just missed out on a kill. Moreover, polar bears can form unusual relationships with other species, including playing with the dogs used to pull sleds in the Arctic. Remarkably, one hand-raised polar bear called Agee has formed a close relationship with her owner Mark Dumas to the point where they even swim together. This is even more astonishing since polar bears are known to actively hunt humans in the wild.

If climate change were to lead to their extinction, this would mean the loss not only of potential breakthroughs in human medicine, but more importantly, the disappearance of an intelligent, majestic animal.
